turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on through. I've done your obs already. Blood pressure 104 over 68, pulse 96, temperature 37.1, oxygen saturation 98 percent. You do look a bit washed out.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I feel shocking. Can we not drag this out? I was up half the night on the loo.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll keep it tight. I'm Dr Nguyen. Tell me what's happened.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Diarrhoea, and I've been vomiting. It kicked off after my cousin's wedding. I blame the prawns.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's not the only one. Her sister messaged, she's got it, and the best man rang this morning crook as well. Same table.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): So a cluster from the one meal. When did it start for you?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Two days. Saturday night, once we got home from the reception.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's not right. You were already pale and running to the toilet Thursday, after the rehearsal dinner. Four days, not two.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday was the rich food sitting funny. The proper runs were Saturday. I'm too tired to relitigate it.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): All right, I'll note it as roughly two to four days, since you two don't land on the same start. How many bowel motions today?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Six, seven, I genuinely lost count after breakfast. It's just brown water.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any blood, or anything black?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the vomiting?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Three times overnight. Last one was about five this morning. I still feel queasy, but I haven't actually thrown up since.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tummy pain with it?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not really. Just the urgency.
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was doubled over in the passenger seat, hand on her belly the whole way down the Monash.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): That was the seatbelt digging in. Leave it.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Any fever, or chills?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I felt hot in the night. Didn't bother with a thermometer. I'm freezing in here now, though. This room is an icebox.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Managing to drink?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Bits of water. It sits all right if I sip it, but my mouth is dry as a chip.

[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I bought Gastrolyte. She wouldn't touch it. But she did take Imodium this morning, and the chemist specifically said not to, because other people from the wedding were sick.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): The chemist isn't the one sprinting to the toilet. Two capsules, 2 milligrams each, about eight o'clock. I'd have another if they were in my handbag.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please don't take any more loperamide. If this is a shared bug, slowing the gut can hang onto it. We'll sort fluids shortly.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. You're the doctor.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any regular tablets? Pressure meds, anything daily?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing regular. A multivitamin some weeks, but not lately.

[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just so it's clear, I'm her husband. I took my own metformin this morning for my diabetes. That's me, not her. Her sister's biotin gummies for her hair have nothing to do with this either.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. I won't put your metformin or her sister's biotin anywhere near her record.

[SEG0032] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Traffic was a nightmare, by the way. Hour and a half, prang before the tunnel. ABC had the cricket on, Australia three for eighty-odd at lunch, Smith scratching around.

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I could not care less about the cricket. We had to cancel the granddaughter's sleepover. She's starting kindy next week, made this ridiculous paper crown, and now Nanna's a write-off. And the storm Tuesday sent the wheelie bins down the street.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Shame about the sleepover. Kindy week comes around fast. Let's finish this so you're not stuck in here.
[SEG0035] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yeah, the bins were halfway to the servo. Sorry. Go on.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): You said no pain. Before I examine you, any dizziness, any headache?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Head's fine. I did go woozy when I stood up for water. Had to sit straight back down.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Actually, no, I was short with you about the pain. It cramps, low down, right before I have to go. Sharp, then it eases off once I've been. Sorry.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's all right. So low abdominal cramps just before a bowel motion, settling after. I'll examine you now.

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lips and tongue are dry. Abdomen is soft, mildly tender across the lower tummy, no guarding. The skin on the back of your hand tents a little. Heart sounds are normal, chest is clear.
[SEG0041] person_1 (NURSE): When I took the pulse it was 96, and she looked flat in the waiting room. No urine sample, so I didn't dip anything.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Can I please lie down? I'm done with sitting.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nearly. Let me read it back. Watery diarrhoea, you lost count around six or seven today, vomiting three times overnight and none since about five, still nauseated, dry mouth, woozy on standing, cramps low down before you go. Others from the wedding are unwell too. You took two 2 milligram loperamide capsules this morning against the chemist's advice. No blood in the stool, no headache. Observations are all right and you're mildly dry on exam. Fair?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. That's the lot. Don't add anything.
[SEG0045] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She has hardly wee'd. Once, this morning, and she told me it was dark.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Just the once, and dark?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Once. I didn't study it, but yeah, it was dark.

[SEG0048] person_3 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a short-lived gastro from that wedding meal, with mild dehydration. I can't completely exclude a bug we'd want a stool test for if this hangs around, but I'm not ordering one today.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): So I just go home and suffer?

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): If the diarrhoea hasn't eased in three days, or if you see blood, then we send a stool sample. Stop the loperamide. Sip oral rehydration solution, little and often, and plain water between. You're aiming for pale wee. If you can't keep fluids down, if the dizziness gets worse, or if the pain moves and stays put, come back sooner. If you're still going in three days, book back with me or your usual GP.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Three days of that salty drink. Fantastic.
[SEG0052] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get the Gastrolyte on the way home. And the Imodium stays in the cupboard.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good plan. Take the afternoon quietly.
[SEG0054] person_1 (NURSE): I'll walk you out and grab a cup of water for the car. Sit down and sing out if you feel faint in the corridor.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): If the corridor spins I'm sitting on the floor. I'm not making a scene, I'm just warning you.

spec.situation: Diarrhoea and vomiting after a trip or a wedding meal; others at the event are ill; patient counts bowel movements loosely; takes loperamide against advice; mild dehydration signs; stool test conditional; advice on fluids.
features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
